rows.claim: defendant A (claim): the stream state graph is endpoint-role symmetric -- swapping the two endpoint roles (local <-> remote) maps every arrow to an arrow: reserved (local) <-> reserved (remote) (server-push reservation twins), half-closed (local) <-> half-closed (remote), with idle, open and closed fixed. The RFC writes the two reserved states and the two half-closed states as mirror bullet lists, and the RST escape says verbatim 'Either endpoint can send a RST_STREAM frame' in both reserved states.
defendant B: half-closed (local) and half-closed (remote) are shape-twins (both drain to closed on three events), so maybe they can be swapped while keeping reserved (local)/(remote) fixed
positive control: padding states 7 and 8 have byte-identical rows (every event self-loops, reward 0), so the swap is a genuine symmetry under BOTH readings and should be admitted everywhere
defendant C: reserved (local) and reserved (remote) are server-push twins (both released by RST from either endpoint), so maybe they can be swapped while keeping the half-closed pair fixed
